inputSentence: The 2026 FIFA World Cup kicks off at Estadio Azteca on June 11, 2026.
heroSummary: The men's World Cup returns with a bigger field, three host countries, and the political as well as sporting complexity that comes with a month-long event spread across North America. This page is designed to track venue milestones, qualification context, and the shape of the tournament before the opening whistle.
whatChanged: With an opening venue and date locked in, the World Cup story moves from abstract anticipation to operational countdown: schedules, stadium readiness, host-city planning, and contenders all become concrete coverage threads.
whyItMatters: This is not just the biggest event in football. It is also an infrastructure story, a travel story, a sponsorship story, and a soft-power story playing out across Mexico, the United States, and Canada.

keyFacts.label: Host countries
keyFacts.value: Canada, Mexico, and the United States

keyFacts.label: Tournament format
keyFacts.value: Expanded field with more matches than previous editions

timeline.title: The joint North American bid wins hosting rights
timeline.description: FIFA awards the tournament to the Canada-Mexico-United States bid, locking in a geographically sprawling World Cup with heavy logistical demands.

timeline.title: Host-city and scheduling details sharpen
timeline.description: As stadium plans and calendar decisions solidify, the story broadens from bid politics to transport, security, and local economic expectations.

timeline.title: Opening match at Estadio Azteca
timeline.description: The tournament begins in one of football's most symbolic stadiums, immediately centering the event in World Cup history as well as present-day competition.

watchItems.title: How the 48-team format feels in practice
watchItems.description: The expansion changes everything from match volume to rest windows and could alter which kinds of national teams gain momentum.

watchItems.title: Stadium and transit readiness
watchItems.description: A multi-country event lives or dies on movement: airports, host-city transport, crowd control, and venue operations are editorially important.

watchItems.title: North American hosting politics
watchItems.description: Cross-border policy, security posture, and visa realities can become as central to coverage as the football itself.

watchItems.title: Contender shape
watchItems.description: As qualifiers end and squads form, the page should shift toward favorites, dark horses, and injury-driven volatility.

entities.name: FIFA
entities.detail: Owns the competition format, commercial structure, and final decisions on scheduling and operational standards.

entities.name: Estadio Azteca
entities.detail: A stadium with deep World Cup symbolism that makes the opening match feel historically loaded before a ball is kicked.

entities.name: Host-city organizers
entities.detail: Local committees are responsible for the practical experience on the ground, from fan travel to venue readiness.

coverageAngles.title: A bigger World Cup changes the product
coverageAngles.description: The expansion is not cosmetic; it changes the volume of games, the distribution of attention, and the commercial scale of the event.

coverageAngles.title: North America as a football stage
coverageAngles.description: This tournament is also a test of how the sport presents itself in markets with different fan cultures and transport habits.

coverageAngles.title: The venue story matters
coverageAngles.description: Stadium renovations, fan access, and local readiness offer concrete reporting opportunities well before the first round ends.

coverageAngles.title: History versus present performance
coverageAngles.description: Coverage can balance the nostalgia of iconic venues and prior World Cups with a more grounded assessment of who can actually win in 2026.

faq.question: Why lead with the opening venue?
faq.answer: Because locking the site of the first match turns a diffuse mega-event into a more tangible story with a symbolic center and a calendar clock.

faq.question: What makes this page different from a standings page?
faq.answer: A topic page packages logistics, narrative, and editorial framing alongside sports information, making it useful before the full match schedule dominates.

faq.question: How should the page evolve once the tournament starts?
faq.answer: It should pivot from pre-event readiness and qualification context to live results, bracket state, breakout players, and knockout-stage stakes.
